subject: Is it possible change data sets through user input on an interactive graph?

messages.author: 1b35e40a9e8b6f05
messages.subject: Is it possible change data sets through user input on an interactive graph?
parts:
Hi everyone,

I've been working with Shiny and R for quite some time now with some professors at my university, but unfortunately I've come across a problem that I haven't been able to solve on my own, so I was hoping someone out there would be able to help me.

Without getting into the nitty gritty statistical details surrounding the applet, the basic purpose that I need for my app is the ability to change what data set appears on the ggplot graph that I have. I've seen tutorials online for how to manage this, but however, those graphs were all static, while this graph needs to be interactive, or reactive I suppose I should say. I've attached a picture of the segment of my applet in question if that helps at all.

While tinkering around with the code, I've found that forcing the change works, through the use of:

baboonData <- read.csv("baboons2.csv")

later on in the code. However, I don't want it to be executed once and then be over. I'd like to have the user select the data set they would like to use, through some means of a sidebar option, and then have the change reflect in the graph. This won't work with simply forcing the data to be one thing. I've tried using if statements and observeEvent to change the dataset, but for whatever reason, as soon as I put the code mentioned above, which resets the data on its own, will no longer work.

Would anyone have an idea of what could be wrong with my code? Any other command, such as resetting other variables later on in my code, will work, but for some reason this dataset remains the same.

Thanks,
Heather

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Is it possible change data sets through user input on an interactive graph?
parts:
You need to use a reactive expression--this is the core of what Shiny reactive programming is about. You can see a simple example here:
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/tree/master/inst/examples/03_reactivity

This example happens to use textual and tabular output, but you'd do the same thing in your case but just have a plotOutput instead of verbatimTextOutput/tableOutput.

I also highly recommend watching the videos on Effective Reactive Programming here:
https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/

Hope that helps!

messages.subject: Re: Is it possible change data sets through user input on an interactive graph?
parts:
Joe,

I appreciate your assistance, however, I've already looked at that example that you included, and I'm still running into errors using that kind of set up. The very first error that I run into is:

Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() : 
  Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive expression or observer.)

While the only code that it's went through to get to this point is:

baboonA <- read.csv("baboons.csv")
baboonM <- read.csv("baboonsM.csv")
baboonF <- read.csv("baboonsF.csv")

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

baboon <- reactive({ switch(input$popSelect, "all" = baboonA, "male" = baboonM, "females" = baboonF) })

vals <- reactiveValues( keeprows = rep(TRUE, nrow(baboon())))

.....

Is nrow simply not allowed on reactive sets? Unfortunately, I kind of need nrow, because as far as I can tell, it's one of the easiest ways for me to start my list of values that they've excluded. 

This is all, of course, assuming that nrow is the only problem I'm facing. Could it be that I've simply constructed my data set wrong?
